conceptZh: 發條樂團面對一口比鼓還大的粥鍋，小喇叭拿大湯勺、大鼓當碗，兩側的熱氣變成「弓」，中間的米粒排成「米」，湊成「粥」。
object: a wind-up animal band with a tiny trumpet, a big drum and a cymbal, facing a huge steaming pot of rice porridge
morph: two bowed steam curls and a heap of rice grains arrange into 弓 米 弓 and form 粥
creativeAngle: 大小失衡：粥鍋比整個樂團還大，小鴨喇叭手拿比自己高的湯勺，兩邊蒸氣彎成「弓」，米粒堆在中間，合成「粥」。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy with a locked frontal camera, bright and cozy, no flashing. Setting: a clean solid pale-peach backdrop with a pale butter floor. The only on-screen text is one bold, saturated chestnut-brown Traditional Chinese glyph 粥, with a bowed 弓 shape on the left, the 米 in the middle and another 弓 on the right, centered, uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with margins. The lead is an original wind-up animal band: a tiny yellow duck with a toy trumpet, a round gray hippo with a big drum, and a pink mouse with a cymbal, each with a spinning key in the back; no real people. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): the band waddles in for a soup break and halts in front of a gigantic round pot of rice porridge that is twice as tall as the hippo; the first spoken 粥 lands as the pot burps a fat bubble and a curl of steam rises. Moment two (1.8-3.4s): the little duck lifts a ladle taller than himself and cannot reach, so the hippo boosts him up on the drum, the ladle swings, and a wave of soft rice sloshes up; the cymbal clashes and the left and right steam curls bend into two clean brown 弓 shapes on each side; the second spoken 粥 lands on the clash. Moment three (3.4-5.0s): the duck dumps a ladleful of rice grains upward, and they flutter down and settle as a tidy 米 between the two 弓 shapes, completing 粥; the hippo's drum, now used as a bowl, catches the last spill, and as the word 喝粥 is spoken the duck and the mouse take big happy slurps through tiny straws, their keys spinning faster. From 5.0-8.0s the glyph 粥 is completely still, unobstructed and crisp in chestnut brown; the three musicians sit in a row at the side, swaying with their bowls and tapping a soft beat on the drum, never touching the strokes. Narration (off-screen only, warm Taiwanese Mandarin, slow, distinct, clear tones, no erhua): the voice says exactly 「粥、粥、喝粥」, read as ㄓㄡ、ㄓㄡ、ㄏㄜ ㄓㄡ, first utterance at about 0.6s, second at about 2.8s, the word at about 4.4s, then stop with no repeats and no extra speech. Only a soft drum tap, a cymbal ting and simmering bubbles under the voice, no background music. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no clutter.

conceptZh: 調皮小老鼠從大鍋裡拉出一條黏黏的白粥絲，拉布拉多警長衝來抓住另一端拔河，兩個越拉越後仰、臉都紅了，粥絲「啵」一聲斷掉，兩人摔坐在地，兩段回彈的粥絲捲成左右兩個「弓」，翻倒的鍋子噴出米粒落成中間的「米」，拼成「粥」。
object: a giant round pot of thick, sticky white rice porridge that stretches like taffy when pulled
morph: the stretched porridge strand snaps in a tug-of-war; the two recoiling ends curl upright into the left and right 弓 and stiffen deep plum, while the tipped pot flings rice grains that settle as the central 米
creativeAngle: 改用拔河模式與指定的小老鼠主角：粥本身的「黏、拉得很長」特性就是拔河的道具，斷掉時的回彈自然變成兩個弓形，米粒落下成「米」，字形由撞擊直接產生；和前一版樂團舀粥的安靜場面完全不同，節奏改成四段快切。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second animated slapstick clip, locked frontal camera, bright and cozy, no flashing. Setting: a clean solid pale-mint backdrop with a pale cream floor, nothing busy behind. The only on-screen text is one bold, saturated deep-plum Traditional Chinese glyph 粥: a bowed 弓 on the left, 米 in the middle, a second 弓 on the right, centered, uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with margins. Cast: an original tiny cheeky cartoon mouse with huge round ears, a skinny whip tail and a permanent grin, and an original big friendly cartoon Labrador sheriff dog with a gold star badge and a whistle. No real people.

Moment one (0.0-1.6s): a giant round pot of thick white rice porridge sits center frame. The mouse pops up at the left rim, eyes sparkling, licks its lips, plunges both paws in and hauls out a long, gooey white porridge strand that stretches like taffy; the first spoken 粥 lands as the strand pulls taut.

Moment two (1.6-3.6s): a whistle toot, and the sheriff charges in from the right, skids straight past the pot, scrambles back, and grabs the far end of the strand to confiscate it. Tug-of-war: both lean further and further back, feet skidding on the cream floor, the strand stretching thinner across the whole frame, the dog's cheeks puffing red, the mouse's tail whipping with glee. A frozen half-second beat: the strand quivers.

Moment three (3.6-5.0s): SNAP with a soft boing. Mouse and sheriff fly backwards and plop onto their bottoms with cartoon squash and a wobble. The two released strand ends recoil, curl upright and stiffen into the deep-plum left and right 弓 shapes; the second spoken 粥 lands exactly as they lock into place. At the same moment the pot tips, flings a spray of rice grains upward, and the grains settle neatly between the bows as the plum 米, completing 粥. The sheriff rubs his head with a dazed grin.

Moment four (5.0-8.0s): the glyph 粥 is completely still, crisp and unobstructed in deep plum. Down in the left corner the mouse holds up a small bowl of smooth white porridge with a tiny spoon, grinning, and the word 白粥 is spoken as the bowl pops into view; the mouse takes a happy wordless slurp while the sheriff, dizzy in the right corner, offers a polite tiny salute. Neither touches the strokes.

Narration (off-screen only, warm Taiwanese Mandarin, slow, distinct, clear tones, no erhua): the voice says exactly 「粥、粥、白粥」, read as ㄓㄡ、ㄓㄡ、ㄅㄞˊ ㄓㄡ, first utterance at about 0.8s, second at about 4.0s, the word at about 5.4s, then stop with no repeats and no extra speech. Only a whistle toot, feet skidding, a soft boing and a cheerful slurp under the voice, no background music. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no clutter.
